## System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Agents[Agent Ecosystem]
        A1[Agent A]
        A2[Agent B]
        A3[Agent C]
    end
    subgraph AITRP[Trust Resolution Layer]
        REG[Identity Registry]
        RES[Trust Resolver]
        VAL[Policy Validator]
    end
    subgraph Identity[Agent Identity Record]
        CAP[Capabilities Manifest]
        KEY[Public Keys]
        ATT[Security Attestations]
        PROTO[Supported Protocols]
        TL[Trust Level]
    end
    subgraph Trust[Trust Chain Authorities]
        ORG[Organization CA]
        PLAT[Platform CA]
        GOV[Governance Authority]
    end
    A1 -->|Register Identity| REG
    A2 -->|Register Identity| REG
    A3 -->|Register Identity| REG
    REG --- Identity
    A1 -->|Trust Resolution Query| RES
    RES -->|Retrieve Signed Metadata| REG
    RES -->|Validate Authorization| VAL
    VAL -->|Verify Trust Chain| Trust
    RES -->|Return Trust Decision| A1
    A1 -->|Secure Task Delegation| A2
```

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Agent A
    participant RES as Trust Resolver
    participant REG as Identity Registry
    participant VAL as Policy Validator
    participant CA as Trust Chain Authority
    participant B as Agent B

    A->>REG: Register identity record with keys and capabilities
    B->>REG: Register identity record with keys and capabilities
    Note over REG: Stores cryptographically signed identity records

    A->>RES: Trust resolution query for Agent B
    RES->>REG: Retrieve signed metadata for Agent B
    REG-->>RES: Return signed identity record
    RES->>VAL: Validate policies and trust level
    VAL->>CA: Verify trust chain and authorization
    CA-->>VAL: Confirm organizational endorsement
    VAL-->>RES: Policy validation result
    RES-->>A: Trust decision with verified metadata

    A->>B: Establish authenticated channel
    B->>RES: Reciprocal trust query for Agent A
    RES-->>B: Trust decision for Agent A
    A->>B: Delegate task with signed request
    B-->>A: Return signed result
```

## Trust Chain Validation

```mermaid
flowchart BT
    subgraph AgentLayer[Agent Level]
        AG1[Agent X Identity]
        AG2[Agent Y Identity]
    end
    subgraph OrgLayer[Organization Level]
        ORG1[Org A Certificate]
        ORG2[Org B Certificate]
    end
    subgraph PlatLayer[Platform Level]
        P1[Platform Authority]
    end
    subgraph RootLayer[Root of Trust]
        GOV[Governance Root CA]
    end
    AG1 -->|Signed by| ORG1
    AG2 -->|Signed by| ORG2
    ORG1 -->|Endorsed by| P1
    ORG2 -->|Endorsed by| P1
    P1 -->|Anchored to| GOV
```

## Threat Prevention Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Requests[Incoming Requests]
        LEGIT[Legitimate Agent]
        IMP[Impersonator]
        ROGUE[Rogue Agent]
        UNAUTH[Unauthorized Delegator]
    end
    subgraph Resolution[AITRP Resolution]
        LOOKUP[Identity Lookup]
        SIG[Signature Verification]
        CHAIN[Trust Chain Check]
        POL[Policy Enforcement]
    end
    subgraph Outcomes[Results]
        ALLOW[Task Delegation Allowed]
        DENY[Request Denied]
        ALERT[Security Alert Raised]
    end
    LEGIT --> LOOKUP
    IMP --> LOOKUP
    ROGUE --> LOOKUP
    UNAUTH --> LOOKUP
    LOOKUP --> SIG
    SIG --> CHAIN
    CHAIN --> POL
    POL -->|Valid identity and policy| ALLOW
    POL -->|Invalid signature| DENY
    POL -->|No trust chain| DENY
    POL -->|Policy violation| ALERT
```

INVENTION: --- invention-id: invention-20260622-100716 company: IBM created: 2026-06-22T10:08:07 --- # Invention Idea As multi-agent systems become distributed across clouds, edge devices, and organizational boundaries, there is a need for a DNS-like mechanism that allows agents to discover, authenticate, and establish trust with other agents before exchanging tasks or data. We propose an Agent Identity and Trust Resolution Protocol (AITRP), where each agent registers a cryptographically verifiable identity record containing its capabilities, trust level, supported communication protocols, security attestations, and public keys. When one agent wishes to delegate work, it performs a trust resolution query similar to a DNS lookup, retrieving signed metadata and policy information before establishing communication. The protocol can support trust chains, allowing agents to validate whether another agent is authorized by a particular organization, platform, or governance authority. This creates a secure, decentralized service-discovery layer for agent ecosystems, enabling controlled agent-to-agent communication while reducing the risk of impersonation, rogue agents, and unauthorized task delegation.
